p-sign.title: AI Sign Language Translator
p-sign.blurb: Real-time sign language detection using Computer Vision and NLP.
p-sign.slotHint: Drop a screenshot of the translator
p-sign.subtitle: Real-time sign language recognition with computer vision and NLP
writeup: The system captures a live camera feed and tracks 21 hand landmarks per hand using MediaPipe Hands. Landmark coordinates are normalized against wrist position and hand scale, then fed into a classifier trained on isolated sign gestures.

A sliding window buffers landmark sequences over roughly 1.2 seconds so the classifier can distinguish static letter signs from short dynamic gestures (motion-based signs like "J" or "Z"). Predictions are smoothed with a majority vote across the window before being emitted as text.

A lightweight NLP layer sits on top of the raw letter/word stream: it corrects common misreads, inserts word boundaries when the hand pauses, and gives basic sentence casing before the transcript is spoken aloud or displayed.

equations.label: Temporal smoothing (majority vote over window W)

p-cafe.title: Gaming Café Management
p-cafe.blurb: Full-stack web app for booking, admin panel, and dashboard.
p-cafe.slotHint: Drop a screenshot of the dashboard
p-cafe.subtitle: Full-stack booking, billing and admin dashboard
writeup: Built to replace a paper logbook at a local gaming café: customers book a station slot, staff check them in, and billing accrues automatically by the minute against a per-station hourly rate.
The admin dashboard gives station occupancy at a glance, daily/weekly revenue, and a simple inventory view for snacks and drinks sold alongside session time.
Session state (idle / active / overdue) is computed server-side on each request rather than polled by a background job, keeping the deployment to a single Django process plus Postgres.

p-plotter.title: Auto Write Plotter
p-plotter.blurb: A pen plotter that writes by hand. Built for precision and fun.
p-plotter.slotHint: Drop a photo of the plotter
p-plotter.subtitle: A pen plotter that reproduces handwriting on paper
writeup: A two-motor CoreXY gantry moves a servo-lifted pen over a fixed sheet. Input text is converted to a stroke path using a single-line ("hairline") font, then to G-code, then interpreted on an Arduino driving two NEMA17 steppers.
The mechanical design prioritizes reduced backlash over top speed — belt tension and pen-lift timing are what limit handwriting fidelity, not step resolution.
Pen-up moves are routed as the shortest connecting path between strokes to keep total plot time down without dragging ink between letters.

p-sched.title: School Scheduler
p-sched.blurb: Smart timetable generator for school classes.
p-sched.slotHint: Drop a screenshot of the scheduler
p-sched.subtitle: Smart timetable generator for school classes
writeup: Given a list of classes, teachers, rooms and constraints (teacher availability, room capacity, subject-period limits), the scheduler searches for a conflict-free weekly timetable.
The core is a constraint-satisfaction search with backtracking, ordered by most-constrained-variable first, which converges much faster than plain brute force on real school-sized inputs.
A simple UI lets an admin adjust constraints and re-run generation, with clashes highlighted directly on the draft timetable rather than buried in a log.

p-syllabus.title: Exam Syllabus Scheduler
p-syllabus.blurb: Plan your syllabus, track progress, and never fall behind.
p-syllabus.slotHint: Drop a screenshot of the tracker
p-syllabus.subtitle: Plan your syllabus, track progress, never fall behind
writeup: Takes a syllabus broken into topics with rough time estimates and an exam date, then distributes daily study targets so every topic is covered with buffer days left before the exam.
Progress is logged daily; if a day is missed, the remaining plan is automatically rebalanced across the remaining days rather than just pushed to the end.
A small SQLite database keeps history across exams so the app can show which subjects tend to slip and need more buffer next time.

p-fluid.title: FlowLab
p-fluid.blurb: Explore fluid dynamics through simulations and visualizations.
p-fluid.subtitle: Exploring fluid dynamics through simulation and visualization
writeup: A 2D incompressible flow solver on a staggered grid, using a projection method: an explicit advection-diffusion step followed by a pressure-correction step that enforces the divergence-free condition.
Visualization renders velocity as streamlines and vorticity as a colormap, letting simple setups like flow past a cylinder or a lid-driven cavity be explored interactively.
Planned next: a semi-Lagrangian advection scheme to allow larger timesteps without the current explicit scheme's CFL restriction.
specs: Solver design in progress, not yet running

p-clubster.title: Clubster
p-clubster.blurb: Reads class timetables and tells clubs when they can actually meet.
p-clubster.slotHint: Drop a screenshot of the Discover feed or the timetable upload screen
p-clubster.subtitle: A scheduler that finds when a whole club is actually free to meet

writeup.text: Most college clubs schedule a meeting by texting a few sections and guessing a time that might work. Clubster replaces the guess: it reads every target section's class timetable, merges everyone's busy hours into one timeline, and surfaces the actual windows an event could use.

Each section's timetable is merged into a single busy interval set with a sweep-line pass. What remains after subtracting the college day becomes the candidate gaps. Gaps are scored by \emph{weighted turnout percentage}, not raw headcount, so a small section at high attendance correctly outranks a large section at low attendance. Members marked \code{required} for an event — officers, organisers — act as a hard filter: a gap where they're unavailable is dropped outright, never just scored lower.
The system suggests. The admin always decides.

items: Timetables are uploaded as a photo or PDF and parsed into structured JSON by an LLM, with an admin preview step before anything is saved.
Events carry three visibility levels: club-only, open to the college, or open to other colleges.
Two clubs booking the same venue or overlapping audience get flagged automatically, with the numbers shown to both admins.

writeup.text: A club that has to remember to schedule is a club that eventually stops meeting.
Code is public on \link{GitHub}{https://github.com/Arnavverma325/clubster}, licensed AGPL-3.0.

equations.label: Weighted turnout score for a candidate gap
